key_insight: This paper introduces ConfSeq, a conformation description language that lets language models work directly with 3D molecular structures. It bridges molecular geometry and AI so models can predict conformers, generate 3D molecules, and represent structures more effectively.
problem_solved: Most AI systems struggle to handle three-dimensional molecular structures in a way that is both learnable by language models and useful for downstream molecular modeling tasks. This work addresses the gap between molecular geometry and sequence-based AI representations.
method: Designs ConfSeq, a language for encoding molecular conformations into a sequence-like format.
Uses this representation to make 3D molecular tasks compatible with language models.
Demonstrates strong performance on conformer prediction, 3D molecular generation, and molecular representation tasks.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners in chemistry and drug discovery, this provides a new way to apply language-model tooling to 3D molecular problems. It could simplify model design while improving access to structure-aware molecular learning.

paper_title: Bridging three-dimensional molecular structures and artificial intelligence with a conformation description language
